name: Variable-Length Child Node Pointers
aliases: Combinations of Child Node Pointer Lengths
definition: A technique in Sparse Voxel DAGs (SVDAG) where child node pointers (PT) have varying bit lengths (8b, 16b, or 32b) to optimize address space usage based on scene size and detail requirements.
summary: Variable-Length Child Node Pointers optimize SVDAG memory by using 8, 16, or 32-bit pointers based on address ranges, reducing overhead at the cost of increased traversal complexity.
